benchmarks/_census/cache/eligible-202609.reason: APPROVED. The existing validator passes aa_lcr.md. The dataset card independently supports the core dataset claims: 100 questions; 30 document sets; 234 documents; 2,979,757 total tokens; 99,325 average tokens per set; the seven category counts; the Apache-2.0 question-set licence; and no licence claim for the public-source document texts: https://huggingface.co/datasets/ArtificialAnalysis/AA-LCR and https://huggingface.co/datasets/ArtificialAnalysis/AA-LCR/raw/main/README.md. The same card confirms v1.1 (September 2026), sixteen corrected answer keys, four substantive answer corrections, the added judge system prompt, unchanged questions/document sets, the v1.0.0 revision, the human first-attempt 40-60% range, the prompt construction and ordered document loading, and the v1.1 equality-checker JSON protocol. Artificial Analysis's methodology independently confirms that v1.1 adds the system prompt, corrects 16 answer keys, uses approximately 100k cl100k_base tokens per question and a minimum 128K context, evaluates 100 questions in seven categories, uses GPT-5.6 Luna medium as the equality checker, and scores pass@1: https://artificialanalysis.ai/methodology/intelligence-benchmarking. It also confirms the 5% General Index weight and v4.2/v4.3 chronology. The official leaderboard independently confirms the long-context scope, 100-question design, multi-document synthesis requirement, current v1.1 label, 28-of-516 coverage, and live Kimi K3 88.7% table while making clear that this live table is distinct from the dated snapshot: https://artificialanalysis.ai/evaluations/artificial-analysis-long-context-reasoning. The v4.2 release article establishes the dated 4 September 2026 release context and the Index update: https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/artificial-analysis-intelligence-index-v4-2. I independently inspected the v4.2 chart image referenced by that article: its AA-LCR v1.1 panel labels GPT-6 Astra (max) 81% and GLM-5.3 (max) 80%, matching the page and evidence record; the rounded values are correctly described as a dated, non-compute-matched pair rather than live scores. The OpenCompass configuration independently confirms AA-LCR, n=3, and the older user-only CORRECT/INCORRECT judge template, while the loader confirms the AA-LCR dataset files, test construction, ordered source filenames, and token field: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-compass/opencompass/main/opencompass/configs/datasets/aa_lcr/aa_lcr_gen.py and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-compass/opencompass/main/opencompass/datasets/aa_lcr.py. The page correctly distinguishes this approximation from official v1.1, states that execution dates and hidden prompt pins are not established, separates live from dated results, records medium contamination risk for public questions/documents, and avoids claiming a random or human baseline in the schema fields. No substantive unsupported conflict was found.
